summary.headline: Phoenix Mills Q2 FY27 annuity EBITDA rose 21% to Rs 669 crore, with retail consumption up 25% and rental income up 15%.
summary.overview: Annuity revenue (retail, offices, hotel, asset management) grew 16% YoY to Rs 1,055 crore in Q2, with annuity EBITDA up 21% to Rs 669 crore and PAT before minority interest up 31% to Rs 391 crore. Consolidated revenue of Rs 1,153 crore was held back by lower residential handovers (Rs 62 crore recognised in H1), with Rs 120 crore of sold units slated for H2. Office occupancy rose to about 79% in September 2026 from 70% in March 2026, and consumption grew 25% with no new retail area added. Management reaffirmed double-digit rental growth for FY28, stated retail rental guidance of 15% for FY27 could be exceeded, and disclosed progress on the ISMDPL stake step-up to 68.1%.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Rental income up 15% to Rs 605 crore in Q2 and 16% to Rs 1,200 crore in H1; retail EBITDA up 18% to Rs 639 crore in Q2. Consumption Rs 4,685 crore (+25%); excluding jewellery and electronics +22%.

segments.name: Offices
segments.commentary: Office income up 64% YoY to Rs 89 crore and EBITDA up similarly to Rs 56 crore in Q2; 54% of the new office portfolio is rent generating against 79% leased.

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: The St. Regis Mumbai income and EBITDA up 13% in Q2, with average room rate up 20% and EBITDA margin at 44%.

segments.name: Residential
segments.commentary: Revenue recognised on handover; only Rs 62 crore in H1 versus a significantly higher prior-year period. Rs 120 crore of sold units to be booked in H2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Retail rental growth guidance of 14-15% for FY27 (given in April) expected to be exceeded by 1-2 percentage points, per management.
Rental growth of 14-15% factored for FY28 as the more tangible metric; double-digit rental growth expected in FY28 from existing assets.
Phoenix Mall of Asia expected to sustain healthy double-digit consumption growth in FY28.
October 2026 consumption expected at least 20% YoY on a normalised basis, with upside toward 25%; full-month figures due late November.
ISMDPL stake to rise from 58.33% to 68.1% on completion of capital reduction, expected November 2026, for Rs 1,350 crore consideration. Credit rating upgrades expected in one to two weeks.
capex_capacity: Kolkata mall: fit-outs to start around Q2 FY27 (calendar), launch about six months later; about 90% leased. Kolkata residential launch expected in about two quarters.
Surat mall: 50% leased, completion by 2027 and opening in 2028. Bengaluru Whitefield retail expansion (1-1.5 lakh sq ft): completion by 2027, about 70% leased.
Palladium (Lower Parel) Rise 1 expansion: about 150 stores, 60% leased, rentals expected above Rs 500 psf pm; mall operational in calendar 2027. Rise offices targeted for 2028.
Thane, Chandigarh and Coimbatore malls targeted for operations in calendar 2030. Bengaluru first-phase office (about 400,000 sq ft) and Grand Hyatt Bangalore hotel to become operational.
Lucknow Palassio adds about 100,000 sq ft (about 100 stores) with a further floor; Palladium adds 150 stores. Land spend H1 about Rs 800 crore, construction spend H1 about Rs 700 crore.
demand_pricing: Consumption up 25% YoY to Rs 4,685 crore in Q2 and 28% to Rs 9,415 crore in H1; every mall delivered double-digit consumption growth.
Trading occupancy rose only about 3 percentage points YoY; management attributed not more than 3% of the 25% growth to added trading area.
Fashion and accessories (about 60% of trading area) +22%; F&B +21%; entertainment +16%.

Phoenix Mall of Asia consumption +68%, rental +44%, trading occupancy 96% vs 84%. Bengaluru MarketCity consumption +19%, rental +25%, occupancy 93% vs 82%. Pune Avenue of Stars consumption +21%, rental +16%, occupancy 90% vs 82%.
Trading density crossed Rs 3,300 psf pm. Rent-to-consumption ratio at 13%, against a long-term range of 13.5-14%.
About 50% of retail area lease expiries fall between FY27 and FY29; repricing typically gives about 20% uplift on prior minimum guarantee rents.
September was seasonally weak; 2-3% of quarterly consumption lost to fit-outs, with 5% of leasable area under active fit-out.

qa_highlights.question: Why is residential at Kolkata not yet launched more than three and a half years after land acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited an initial plan change from a different use to pure residential and approval delays linked to elections; launch expected in about two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pre-leasing status of upcoming malls (Kolkata, Surat, Bengaluru, Palladium)?
qa_highlights.answer: Kolkata about 90% leased, Surat 50%, Bengaluru expansion about 70%, Palladium Rise 1 about 60%.

qa_highlights.question: Is October consumption growth tracking?
qa_highlights.answer: Normalised for Diwali timing, October is expected at least 20% YoY, possibly toward 25%; final figures due late November.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 rental growth exceed the 15% guidance given the 16% H1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects guidance to be raised by 1-2 percentage points and is optimistic it can be exceeded, pending festive-season data.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 10-city pipeline raise the 1 million sq ft annual addition guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said land is not yet secured for the new cities, so no timelines or guidance change; new cities expected in the 2035-36 plan. Benchmark per new mall moves to 1.3-1.4 million sq ft.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs 1,440 crore H1 capex in the cash flow reconcile with lower construction spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Difference is land: Chandigarh land completion payment of about Rs 700 crore in Q1, plus smaller Coimbatore and Kolkata parcels and an advance for an acquisition under discussion.

risks_watch: Consumption growth moderating against a higher base from Q3 FY27; trading occupancy churn at Palassio, Indore and MarketCity Mumbai.
Residential revenue lumpiness; Rs 120 crore of sold units to be recognised in H2 FY27.
Office leasing conversion: 79% leased but only 54% rent generating; targets of 70% by March and 80% by mid-2027.
Pending acquisition with advance already paid; undisclosed size and timing.
Credit rating upgrades and ISMDPL capital reduction completion expected November 2026.
Management declined to guide beyond FY28 rental growth.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating momentum and the rental growth outlook, but guarded on consumption and beyond FY28, deferring new-city and volume-driven projections. Several answers on the land pipeline and new-city timelines were non-committal.
key_quotes: Importantly, this growth is being driven by improving performance across our existing operational portfolio and with no new (mall) addition to this portfolio for the last two years.
Consumption is driven by many factors, whether gold prices or electronics or some new stores or categories doing well or not doing well.
I am optimistic that the guidance of 15% that we gave, we should be able to cross it.

growth.why: Management raised FY27 retail rental growth guidance by 1-2 pts above ~15% (FY27 guide 14-15% from April) and held FY28 at 14-15%, backed by H1 rental up 16%, Q2 consumption up 25%, and trading occupancy at 96%; new capacity (Palladium Rise 1, Lucknow, Bengaluru office/retail, Surat) is largely 2-4 quarters out and only partly leased.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Annuity EBITDA rose 21% against annuity revenue up 16% (Q2 Rs 669 crore), and as lease repricing of about 20% uplift on expiring minimum guarantees (about 50% of area expires FY27-FY29) flows through, operating leverage should continue.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Palladium Rise 1 (about 150 stores, 60% leased) and Lucknow Palassio (about 100,000 sq ft) are under construction for Q2-Q4 FY27 operation, Bengaluru office (about 400,000 sq ft) and Whitefield retail land in Q4 FY27 to 2027, and Surat opens in 2028 at 50% leased.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Consumption grew 25% in Q2 and 28% in H1 with no new retail area added (trading occupancy up only about 3 points), and management expects at least 20% in October on a normalised basis, with rental growth at 14-15% for FY28.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Trading occupancy is at 96% (up from 84%), but management has no new-city land secured and H1 capex of Rs 1,440 crore is already committed to existing malls, so new capex is more likely to be land or pipeline approvals than a fresh project announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said FY27 retail rental growth guidance should be raised by 1-2 points from about 15% (H1 rental up 16%, Q2 consumption up 25%), with the formal revision likely at the next update.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 rental growth is 16% against FY27 guidance of 14-15%, with management expecting to beat it by 1-2 points; October consumption is tracking at least 20% YoY, though Q3 base effects and churn at Palassio, Indore and MarketCity Mumbai are a watch item.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Palladium Rise 1 expansion (about 150 stores, 60% leased, operational calendar 2027) and Lucknow Palassio (about 100 stores) are scheduled to open in the window, with the Kolkata residential launch expected in about two quarters.

rows.label: Kolkata mall 90% leased; Kolkata residential launch
rows.why: Kolkata mall is about 90% leased with fit-outs starting around Q2 FY27 and launch about six months later, and the Kolkata residential launch is expected in about two quarters.

rows.label: ISMDPL stake step-up to 68.1%
rows.why: Stake rises from 58.33% to 68.1% on completion of capital reduction for Rs 1,350 crore, with credit rating upgrades expected in one to two weeks.

rows.label: Lease repricing on expiring minimum guarantees
rows.why: About 50% of retail lease expiries fall between FY27 and FY29, and repricing typically gives about 20% uplift on prior minimum guarantee rents, with rent-to-consumption at 13% against a 13.5-14% long-term range.
